title: Detached HEAD: you are not lost, you are just not on a branch
summary: Check out a commit directly, make work there, then watch it become unreachable — and recover it. The scariest message in git turns out to be one sentence of theory.
mental_model: Normally HEAD points at a branch, and the branch points at a commit. Detached means HEAD points straight at a commit, skipping the branch. Commits still work — but nothing follows you, so the moment you leave, your new commits have no name.
danger: Committing on a detached HEAD and then switching away leaves those commits reachable only through the reflog. They are garbage-collected eventually.

steps.title: See the normal arrangement first
steps.why: `.git/HEAD` literally contains `ref: refs/heads/main`. That indirection is what 'being on a branch' means — there is no other magic.

steps.title: Detach on purpose
steps.why: Checking out a tag or a raw sha points HEAD at the commit itself. This is completely normal — CI does it on every build — and the warning git prints is informational, not an error.
steps.expect: HEAD now holds a raw sha, and app.py reads 1.0.

verify.label: HEAD is detached (it points at a commit, not a ref)

steps.title: Commit anyway — it works
steps.why: Committing while detached is legal. HEAD moves forward to the new commit. What is missing is any branch trailing behind it, which is the entire problem in one sentence.

actions.run: git commit -q -m "Emergency hotfix on the 1.0 line"

steps.expect: Your commit exists but carries no branch label in the graph.

steps.title: Walk away and lose it
steps.why: Switching back to main moves HEAD to the branch. The hotfix commit is now referenced by nothing — it does not show in `git log --all`, and it is on the clock for garbage collection.
steps.expect: The hotfix is nowhere in --all output.

steps.title: Find it again
steps.why: The reflog recorded every position HEAD held, including the detached ones. `git log --graph --oneline HEAD@{1}` shows the commit is still perfectly intact in the object database.
steps.expect: The hotfix commit, listed with its sha.

steps.title: Give it a name
steps.why: A branch is just a name for a commit. Creating one at that sha makes the work reachable again — and this is exactly what `git switch -c` does for you if you remember to run it *before* leaving.

verify.label: the orphaned commit has a branch again

steps.title: The way to do it deliberately
steps.why: If you know you want to work from an old point, branch at the moment you check it out. `git switch -c <name> <ref>` detaches and re-attaches in one step, so there is never a window where your work is unnamed.

verify.label: you finished back on a real branch
HEAD is attached to a branch again
the commit made while detached was rescued onto a branch
verify.hint: find it in git reflog, then git branch hotfix/1.0 <sha>

verify.label: you also created a branch the safe way, at checkout time
main was never disturbed by any of it

pitfalls: The detached-HEAD warning is not an error. CI systems, `git bisect` and `git rebase` all run detached by design.
`git switch -c <name>` with no ref branches from where you are — the fastest rescue when you notice mid-work that you are detached.
Unreachable commits survive for `gc.reflogExpireUnreachable` (90 days by default), then really are deleted.
`git log --all` deliberately excludes unreachable commits. Use `git reflog` or `git fsck --lost-found` to see them.
cheatsheet: tells you plainly when you are detached
name your current position, attaching HEAD
branch from a point without ever detaching
give an orphaned commit a name
